newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Business sector sees decline in Israeli exports.
newsitem.headline: Business sector sees decline in Israeli exports.

text.p: Israel's business sector expects a decline in exports in the first-quarter of 1997 for the first time in six years, the Manufacturers' Association said on Sunday.
A poll of 200 factories also pointed to a record decline in domestic sales and a drop in production, the association said in a statement.

Fifty-one percent of those polled said their domestic sales had dropped to 1989 levels when Israel last experienced a recession. Fifty-five percent of factories reported either a drop or a sharp drop in production.
Official first-quarter trade figures are expected to be released later this week.

Businessmen expected a slight recovery next quarter, according to the poll. Thirty-seven percent of those surveyed forecast a rise in exports compared with 23 percent who said the decline would continue.
After five years of rapid economic growth, Israel's economy is experiencing a slowdown which some analysts say may lead to a recession.
The business sector has complained that the Bank of Israel's high interest rates, aimed at curbing inflation, have hampered economic activity.
